newsitem.title: USA: U.S health office warn tuna can contain sulfites.
newsitem.headline: U.S health office warn tuna can contain sulfites.

text.p: Asthmatics and other people sensitive to sulfites should temporarily avoid canned tuna, which may contain sulfites, federal health officials said Friday.
The Food and Drug Administration said people with these sensitivities should not eat any white (albacore) canned tuna until the sulfite problem is resolved, which should be soon.
Since some light tunas can also contain sulfites, these people should check with the industry's information number, 1-800-283-1112, before eating them.

The tuna industry said that sulfites had been added without their knowledge to a raw material -- a vegetable protein -- used in canning tuna. The FDA said the industry and the National Food Processors Association had advised them of the problem Thursday.

Nancy Glick, a spokeswoman for the U.S. Tuna Foundation, said that by next week, labels or stickers would be put on cans with sulfites. In "a very short period of time" the tuna will again be sulfite-free, she said.
"Only a handful of people are affected by this, but we're erring on the side of caution," she said.
Sulfites can cause severe, even life-threatening reactions in some asthmatics and people with sensitivity. The amount in tuna will not hurt other people, the FDA said.
Sulfites are used in many foods as a preservative but manufacturers must declare that on the label.
